AssuranceProfile.description:
The assurance boundary the runtime file declares for its seals. The
member and the values are Evidence's.

oneOf.description:
Seals sign with a `local-jwk` key file and are test seals: documents
print them as test seals (`signing.testOnly` is true).
Seals sign through Transit: `signing.testOnly` is false.

AuditDestinationKind.description: The configured audit destination kind, as written in product configuration.

oneOf.description: One JSON line per entry on standard output, flushed per entry.

AuditRuntime.description:
The audit block every Registry Stack product shares: a `file` (the
default) or `stdout` destination, with rotation and retention for a file.

path.description: The absolute path of the active audit file, for a `file` destination.

retentionDays.description: Days a rotated file is kept, for a `file` destination. Default: 90.

rotateBytes.description:
Size at which the active file rotates, in bytes, for a `file`
destination. Default: 100 MiB.

apiKeyRef.description:
Secret reference to the caller API key, under a declared provider.
Omit when OIDC authentication is configured.

Digest.description: A SHA-256 digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

EnvironmentSecretProviderConfig.description: The environment secret provider. It takes no settings.

ExternalId.description: An identifier another system issues, written exactly as its issuer gives it.

root.description:
Absolute directory holding one file per secret. Each file must be a
regular file owned by the runtime user, mode 0400 or 0600, with exactly
one hard link.

JwksSource.description: Where a runtime obtains the OIDC issuer's signing keys.

oneOf.description: Read `jwks_uri` from the issuer's OpenID Connect discovery document.

Fetch the key set from this absolute `https` URI, skipping discovery.
A plain `http` URI is accepted on loopback for supervised local
development, and beyond loopback only when the issuer block sets
`allowInsecureHttp`.

Read the key set from a secret, for deployments without network access
to the issuer.

maximumConcurrentRenders.description: Most renders in flight at once. Default: the CPU count, at most 8.

maximumOutputBytes.description: Largest PDF a render may produce, in bytes.

maximumRequestBytes.description:
Largest request body (data and base64 assets), in bytes. The httpsec
default is 1 MiB; renders with photos need a conscious, bounded raise.

renderTimeoutSeconds.description:
Wall-clock budget per render, in seconds; the worker is killed at
this bound.

ListenerBind.description: Socket address the runtime listens on, written host:port with an IP address host ([addr]:port for IPv6).

ListenerNetworkExposure.description: The operator-declared private network placement of an HTTP listener.

bind.description:
Loopback, private, or link-local address to listen on. A public or
all-interfaces bind is refused when the file is read. TLS is the
proxy's job, not Render's.

shutdownGraceMilliseconds.description:
Time allowed for renders and seals in flight to finish at shutdown,
in milliseconds. Open connections get the same again.

LocalId.description: A local identifier: a lowercase letter, then up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, `_`, or `-`.

anyOf.description: Admit a token from every client the issuer verifies.
Admit a token only from a listed client.

OidcAllowedClients.description:
How `allowedClients` is written (CFG-EMPTY-2): the keyword `unrestricted`,
or a list of at least one client. An empty list is refused, because it
reads as both "none" and "any".

OidcRuntime.description: Serving-adapter OIDC configuration. The pure rendering library never reads it.

allowInsecureHttp.description:
Permit plain HTTP beyond loopback to the configured issuer and to a
JWKS URI declared in configuration. TLS remains required unless the
operator explicitly accepts this transport risk.

allowedClients.description:
The OAuth clients whose access tokens are admitted: `unrestricted` to
admit a token from every client the issuer verifies, or a list of at
least one distinct client. A runtime decides whether `unrestricted`
is acceptable in production.

assertionIssuers.description:
Assertion authorities each client may exchange a subject token from,
keyed by client identifier. Omitted, no assertion-issuer rule applies;
written, it lists at least one client, each with at least one
authority. Once a client is listed, a token it exchanged is accepted
only for one of that client's declared authorities, and a client that
is not listed may exchange from no authority.

audience.description: The audience every accepted access token must carry in `aud`.

issuer.description:
Exact issuer accepted in access-token `iss` claims, an absolute
`https` URL, or a plain `http` URL when `allowInsecureHttp` is set.

jwksSource.description:
Where the issuer's signing keys come from. Absent reads the issuer's
OpenID Connect discovery document.

PackageConfig.description:
The package a runtime serves: `root` is the absolute package directory,
and `expectedDigest`, when set, pins the package digest the runtime must
find there. The package digest is the digest of the package's
`SHA256SUMS` file; see [`crate::package`].

expectedDigest.description:
`sha256:` label of the package digest, the digest of the package's
`SHA256SUMS` file. When set, the runtime refuses to start on any other
package.

root.description: Absolute path of the package directory.

SealRuntime.description:
One seal: the signer, the certificate chain, the timestamp policy, and
the clients allowed to use it.

allowedClients.description:
The OIDC clients allowed to seal with this seal: a list of at least
one client, each also admitted by `authentication.oidc.allowedClients`. There is
no `unrestricted` form and no wildcard: a seal issues documents in the
institution's name, so every seal-capable client is named. Keep these
clients separate from any citizen-facing client.

certificateChainFile.description:
Absolute path of the PEM certificate chain file, the seal's own
certificate first, then each issuer. It is absolute like Render's
other runtime paths, so a runtime file names deployment locations,
not locations relative to wherever the file was copied.

signer.description:
Binds the seal to the private-key transport that produces its
signature. Selects the signer transport for this seal: `local-jwk`
resolves a file-provider secret directly, `transit` calls a
workload-local Transit signing proxy over a Unix socket. Under
`assuranceProfile: production` a seal signs through `transit` only;
under `local` it signs with a `local-jwk` key file only.

timestampAuthority.description:
The RFC 3161 timestamp authority that timestamps each seal (PAdES
B-T), so the seal keeps validating after its certificate expires.
Exactly one of `timestampAuthority` and `withoutTimestamp` is
required.

withoutTimestamp.description:
Seal without a timestamp (PAdES B-B). The only value states the
consequence the operator accepts: a seal without a timestamp stops
validating when its certificate expires, which is usually before the
document stops mattering. Exactly one of `timestampAuthority` and
`withoutTimestamp` is required.

SealSignerRuntime.description:
The private-key transport a seal signs through. The `type` member names
the variant.

oneOf.description: Resolves a file-provider secret directly; for `assuranceProfile: local`.

privateKeyRef.description:
Names the file-provider secret holding the local signing private
key material, read only when `signer.type` is `local-jwk`; the
value is a reference, and configuration never carries the key
bytes themselves. The secret is one private JSON Web Key, the
form `registry-render keygen` writes.

oneOf.description:
Calls a workload-local Transit signing proxy over a Unix socket. The
key is an ECDSA P-256 Transit key, so the seal signs ES256, and it
never leaves Transit.

attemptTimeoutMilliseconds.description:
Bounds how long the runtime waits on each call to the Transit
signing proxy; because a `transit` signer keeps no local fallback
key, a call that exceeds this bound fails the seal request rather
than blocking it indefinitely.

keyVersion.description:
Pins signing to one exact Transit key version rather than a
`latest` alias, so a provider-side rotation cannot silently
replace the key bytes behind an unchanged seal certificate.

mount.description:
Names the Transit secrets-engine mount this signer calls; it is a
path segment in the local Transit-proxy request URL, not a
filesystem location.

unixSocketPath.description:
Absolute Unix socket path used to reach the workload-local Transit
signing proxy; the runtime supplies no provider token over this
connection, because token custody and renewal stay with the proxy.

SecretProvidersConfig.description:
The secret providers a runtime enables. A reference is resolved only by a
provider declared here: `secret:file/name` under `file.root`, and
`secret:env/NAME` only when `environment: {}` is present.

environment.description:
Enables `secret:env/NAME` references, read from the process
environment. Declared as an empty mapping: `environment: {}`.

file.description: Enables `secret:file/name` references, read from files under `root`.

SecretReference.description: An exact secret reference: secret:file/name, resolved under secretProviders.file.root, or secret:env/NAME, resolved only when secretProviders.environment is declared.

SigningRuntime.description:
Document sealing: the seals this deployment can apply. A seal is a PAdES
signature made with the institution's own key. Which document types use
which seal is decided in the bundle manifest (`seal` on a document type),
never by the caller.

seals.description:
The seals, keyed by the local identifier the bundle manifest's `seal`
names. At least one seal is required: omit `signing` to turn sealing
off.

TimestampAuthorityRuntime.description: The RFC 3161 timestamp authority a seal uses.

attemptTimeoutMilliseconds.description: Time allowed for one request to the authority, in milliseconds.

caBundleRef.description:
PEM CA bundle for the authority. Omitted, the platform's trusted
roots verify it.

url.description:
Absolute `https` URL of the authority. `http` is accepted only for a
loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`), for a test
authority on the same machine.

Url.description: An absolute http or https URL with a host preserved as written, no user information, and no backslash, whitespace or control character. DNS case and equivalent IPv6 literals are permitted.

WithoutTimestamp.description: The acknowledgement a seal needs to go without a timestamp.

oneOf.description:
The seal carries no timestamp, so it stops validating when its
certificate expires.

ipv4SocketHost.description: Four canonical decimal IPv4 octets followed by a decimal port.

ipv6HexSocketHost.description: A bracketed hexadecimal IPv6 literal, including every RFC 3986 compression position, followed by a decimal port.

ipv6MixedSocketHost.description: A bracketed IPv6 literal whose final 32 bits use canonical dotted-decimal IPv4 notation, followed by a decimal port.

socketPort.description: A decimal u16 port, including zero and Rust-compatible leading zeroes.

assuranceProfile.description:
The assurance boundary of this deployment's seals, the same member
and values Evidence declares. Required when `signing` declares a
seal, and unused otherwise. `local` signs with a `local-jwk` key
file and marks every seal a test seal; `production` signs through
`transit` only, so a production key never leaves Transit.

package.description: The verified bundle package Render serves.

secretProviders.description:
Providers for secret references. Omit when the authentication mode uses
no secret references.

signing.description:
Optional document sealing. Omit it and Render loads no signer, makes
no timestamp call, and cannot seal any document.
